- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in the early part of the forecast horizon (first 10–15 days).
- Overshoots after sharp upward spikes in the history (e.g., after 77.5+ values), then corrects downward — model lags in recognizing the peak’s end.
- Mean reversion tendency: model tends to overcorrect downward after overestimating, but fails to fully revert to historical mean in the final 5–10 days.
- Forecast bias is higher in the first 10 days, then stabilizes or slightly underestimates later — suggests model is too aggressive in early periods.
- Model underestimates true price peaks in the final 5–10 days, especially when true values are rising sharply — indicates horizon mismatch or delayed response to new data.
- Model exhibits “late correction” behavior — true values often exceed forecast by 1–2% in the last 5–10 days, suggesting model is not fully adaptive to recent trends.
